subsystems.name: Warm-water intake
subsystems.role: feeds surface seawater at roughly 25 °C into the evaporator.

subsystems.name: Cold-water pipe
subsystems.role: reaches down 600–1000 m for water at around 4–5 °C — the single hardest piece of the plant.
parts: long large-diameter HDPE or composite pipe

subsystems.name: Heat exchangers
subsystems.role: evaporate and condense the working fluid across a very small temperature difference, so they must be enormous.

subsystems.name: Power loop
subsystems.role: turns the vapour pressure difference into electricity.

subsystems.name: Platform or shore plant
subsystems.role: houses the machinery — either on land beside deep water or on a moored floating hull.

subsystems.name: Export and co-product system
subsystems.role: delivers power to shore and exploits the cold water for other uses.

buildSteps.title: Select the site
buildSteps.detail: Map the temperature profile with depth and confirm at least about 20 °C difference reachable within a short distance of a steep seabed, typically in the tropics.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the cold-water pipe
buildSteps.detail: Long lengths of large-diameter plastic or composite pipe are made on shore, fitted with a weighted intake head, and floated ready for towing.

buildSteps.title: Build the plant
buildSteps.detail: A moored floating hull is assembled, or a shore station is built at a site where deep water comes close to land.

buildSteps.title: Install the heat exchangers
buildSteps.detail: Very large evaporator and condenser banks are fitted with corrosion-resistant tubes and access for cleaning.

buildSteps.title: Sink and connect the cold-water pipe
buildSteps.detail: The pipe is towed to site, sunk under controlled ballasting, connected to the plant's cold-water pump, and its intake positioned at depth.

buildSteps.title: Charge the power loop
buildSteps.detail: The closed loop is filled with working fluid and the turbine-generator commissioned.

buildSteps.title: Commission and manage fouling
buildSteps.detail: Warm and cold flows are ramped up while operators watch for biological growth, corrosion and the effect of storms on the pipe.

buildSteps.title: Deliver power and co-products
buildSteps.detail: Electricity goes ashore by subsea cable; the spent cold water can feed desalination or aquaculture.

prerequisites.tech: Long deep-water pipes surviving at sea
prerequisites.why: pipes reaching about 1000 m have worked in pilot plants, but a storm-resilient, cheap version at full scale is unproven.
a temperature difference of only 20 °C means vast surface area and high parasitic pumping losses.
the oil and gas industry already builds and moors large hulls in deep water.
power must reach a coastal grid, often from several kilometres offshore.

prerequisites.tech: Corrosion and biofouling control in warm seawater
prerequisites.why: tropical seawater attacks tubes and grows films that blunt heat transfer.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants of roughly 100 kW or less on tropical coasts and islands, often sharing a site with aquaculture or desalination
pathway.unlocks: real operating data on pipes, heat exchangers and fouling.

pathway.milestone: pre-commercial plants of a few megawatts serving island grids
pathway.unlocks: a credible cost comparison with diesel generation on remote islands.

pathway.milestone: floating plants that make power, fresh water or hydrogen offshore
pathway.unlocks: marine energy for places with no suitable coastal shelf.
firm, round-the-clock baseload power from the ocean's temperature gradient.
